neighbours.label: 'So' or 'That' at the start of a sentence that picks up what was just said ('So let me say ...', 'That problem: ...'); plain continuations stay quiet
fire:
I answered badly at the interview.
So let me try again here.

The old theory has a big flaw.
So what should replace it?
Prices have doubled this year. So, for instance, rents are high.
There is a serious gap in the plan. That gap being money.
We studied one more problem. That problem: rising seas.

Nobody read the first report.
So here is a short summary.
He founded the town in 1676. That year, the river flooded.

You asked me about taxes.
So here is my answer.
quiet:
I answered badly at the interview.
I went home by bus.

The old theory has a big flaw.
The new one does not.
Prices have doubled this year. Rents are high.
There is a serious gap in the fence near my house.
We studied one more problem. The rising seas were next.

Nobody read the first report.
The second came in May.
He founded the town in 1676. The river flooded.

You asked me about taxes.
I paid them in June.

notes: Card: ' so' x13, ' So' x6, 'So' x3, ' That' x3, ' therefore' x2. The - pole has the same words. Probe: 'So let me say' after a new line 0.55, '. That hole being' 0.46, 'So, for example' 0.13; 'so close that' 0.10, 'tired, so' 0.09, plain sentences 0.01-0.07. Uneven; I expect a marginal result.
